lauds:
Welcome. I’m glad you’re here. Before the day asks anything of you, take a breath and make a little room for God.

The Breviary, also called the Liturgy of the Hours, is the Church’s daily prayer. At its heart are the Psalms: prayers Jesus prayed, and prayers the Church has carried through every kind of day. When we pray them, we don’t have to find perfect words of our own. We join a prayer larger than ourselves, bringing our gratitude, our worries, and our hope with us.

The full prayer of the Church includes several psalms and readings at each hour. Soundfaith offers a simpler way to begin: one psalm each day, with the other parts of the prayer gathered around it. Take your time. You can pause, listen, or return to a line that stays with you.

Lauds is Morning Prayer. Traditionally prayed at daybreak, it gives the day to God before it fills with everything else. Whether you’re just waking, already on your way, or finding a quiet moment later, you’re welcome here.

As we begin, hold one part of the day in your heart. What would you like to place in God’s hands? Let’s pray Lauds together.
vespers:
Welcome. I’m glad you’ve made a little space for prayer. Take a slow breath and let the day settle for a moment. Whatever it held—good news, hard work, an unfinished task—you can bring it with you.

Vespers is Evening Prayer. As the light begins to fade, the Church gathers to give thanks for the day and entrust the night to God. You don’t need to have everything sorted out before you begin. Let the psalm give voice to whatever is in your heart, and rest in the knowledge that God is near.

Let’s pause together and pray Vespers.
compline:
Welcome. I’m glad you’re here at the close of the day. Take a breath. You can set down, for now, the things you could not finish and the things you cannot change.

Compline is Night Prayer, the last prayer of the day. The Church entrusts the night to God, asking for peace and placing our cares in his hands. As you pray, let the words quiet your heart. You are held through the night, and tomorrow can begin in its own time.

Let’s end the day gently and pray Compline.
